primitives.name: Shannon entropy of a discrete source (Theorem 2 axiomatic characterization)
primitives.verbatim_quote: We shall call H - ~ Pi log Pi the entropy of the set of proba- bilities PI, ... ,Pn. If x is a chance varIable we wIll wflte H (x) for its entropy; thus x is not an argument of a function but a label for a number, to differentiate it from H(y) say, the entropy of the chance variable y. The entropy in the case of two possibilities with probabilities P and q = 1 - P, namely H = - (p log P + q log q) is plotted in Fig. 7 as a function of p. The quantity H has a number of interesting properties which further substantiate it as a reasonable measure of choice or information. 1. H = 0 if and only if all the Pi but one are zero, this one having the value unity. Thus only when we are certain of the out- come does H vanish. Otherwise H is positive. 2. For a given n, H is a maximum and equal to log n when all the Pi are equal
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H = entropy, bits (log base 2; base e gives natural units, base 10 decimal digits, printed p.32-33); p_i = probability of symbol/state i, dimensionless probability measure with sum_i p_i = 1; i = index over the n symbols of the finite alphabet; n = alphabet size, dimensionless count; log_2 = binary logarithm, dimensionless. For a finite-state Markov source the per-symbol rate is H = sum_i P_i H_i with P_i the stationary state probability (dimensionless) and H_i the state-conditional entropy (bits/symbol); per-second rate H' = m H with m = average symbols per second (1/s), giving bits/s (printed p.53).
primitives.assumptions: Discrete finite alphabet; probabilities known. Theorem 2 (printed p.49) requires exactly three axioms: (1) H continuous in the p_i; (2) for equal p_i = 1/n, H monotonic increasing in n; (3) grouping: a choice decomposed into successive choices has H equal to the weighted sum of the component H's. Source-rate identification with time averages additionally assumes an ergodic Markoff source (printed p.47-48: graph strongly connected and gcd of circuit lengths = 1).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Continuous distributions: differential entropy is coordinate-relative, can be negative, and shifts by the expected log-Jacobian under change of variables (printed p.90-91); only entropy differences are invariant. Non-ergodic/mixed sources: sequence averages do not equal ensemble averages; the source decomposes into pure components L = sum P_i L_i (printed p.47-48). Degenerate p_i -> 0 handled by continuity (0 log 0 = 0 limit); H = 0 iff one outcome has probability 1. Unknown or non-stationary probabilities void the rate estimate.

layer2.mapping: The offensive call sheet is a finite-state Markoff source: states = (down, distance, field zone, hash, personnel), emitted symbol = play concept. H = sum P_i H_i is the entropy rate of the call distribution in bits/call; relative entropy vs the maximum-entropy source on the same alphabet measures how predictable the scheme is, and 1 minus it is the redundancy a defense can exploit. This is a declared isomorphism of source structure, not a claim that the theorem originates in football.
layer2.telemetry: Internal charting of call sequences (formation, concept, personnel, down/distance/zone) across games; estimate state-conditional symbol frequencies and stationary state occupancy; report H in bits/call with sample-size confidence bounds. No sportsbook inputs.

primitives.name: Equivocation and rate of transmission R = H(x) - H_y(x); noisy-channel capacity C = max[H(x) - H_y(x)]
primitives.verbatim_quote: Following this idea the rate of actual transmission, R, would be obtained by subtracting from the rate of production (i.e., the entropy of the source) the average rate of conditional entropy. R = H(x) - Hy(x) The conditional entropy Hy(x) will, for convenience, be called the equivocation It measures the average ambiguity of the re- eeived signal.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R = rate of actual transmission, bits/symbol or bits/s (basis stated per use); H(x) = entropy of the source/channel input x, bits; H_y(x) = equivocation = conditional entropy of input x given received signal y, bits; x = transmitted message (chance variable label, not a function argument, printed p.51); y = received signal; p(x) = input distribution over which the maximum is taken (dimensionless probability measure); C = channel capacity, bits/s. Identity chain H(x,y) = H(x) + H_x(y) = H(y) + H_y(x) (printed p.66) keeps all terms in bits.
primitives.assumptions: Discrete channel with stationary transition probabilities p_i(j) (probability transmitted i is received as j), possibly finite-state (printed p.65-66); transmitter non-singular so source entropy equals channel-input entropy; maximum over all input sources. The correction-channel interpretation (Theorem 10, printed p.68) assumes an auxiliary observer who sees both sent and received messages.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Naive error-count subtraction fails: with 1% errors the rate is 1000 - 81 = 919 bits/s, not 990, because error locations are unknown (printed p.67); when output is independent of input, half the symbols match by chance yet R = 0 (coin-flip limit, printed p.67-68). Continuous case: H(x) - H_y(x) can assume the indeterminate form infinity - infinity; the integral mutual-information form (Appendix 7, printed p.98, 123-124) is the well-defined generalization.

layer2.mapping: Coverage-read channel: x = true post-snap coverage assignment (latent), y = pre-snap observable shell. The defense's disguise programs the transition table p_i(j); the quarterback's usable read information is R = H(x) - H_y(x), where H_y(x) is computed from the confusion matrix of (pre-snap shell label, post-snap revealed coverage). A disguise that makes the shell independent of the true coverage drives R to 0 even though the QB still 'sees' a shell - the coin-flip limit transposed. The kernel is derived by instantiating Shannon's channel model on charted read pairs.
layer2.telemetry: Charted (pre-snap shell, post-snap coverage) pairs from internal film/tracking data; empirical confusion matrix and its conditional entropy in bits/read; QB time-to-throw as the delay budget. Calibration is against revealed coverage, never against outcomes or odds.

primitives.name: Theorem 11 - Fundamental theorem for a discrete channel with noise (noisy-channel coding theorem)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 11: Let a discrete channel have the capacity C and a discrete source the entropy per second H. If H < C there exists a coding system such that the output of the source can be trans- mitted over the channel with an arbitrarily small frequency of errors (or an arbitrarily small equivocation). If H > C it is pos- sible to encode the source so that the equivocation is less than H - C + f. where f. is arbitrarily small. There is no method of encoding which gives an equivocation less than H - C.
primitives.latex: H < C \;\Rightarrow\; \forall\,\epsilon > 0\ \exists\ \text{code with error frequency} < \epsilon; \qquad H > C \;\Rightarrow\; H_y(x) \ge H - C
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H = source entropy rate, bits/s; C = channel capacity, bits/s; H_y(x) = equivocation (residual uncertainty of the message after reception), bits/s; epsilon = target error frequency, dimensionless probability; the bound H - C is bits/s, dimensionally consistent with H_y(x). The theorem's second clause also states achievability of equivocation < H - C + epsilon for arbitrarily small epsilon (bits/s).
primitives.assumptions: Discrete channel with capacity C defined as max[H(x) - H_y(x)]; discrete source with entropy rate H; block duration T -> infinity (unbounded coding delay); proof is a random-coding existence argument - average error over the ensemble of codes is shown < epsilon, hence at least one good code exists (printed p.71-74). No explicit construction is provided.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Finite block length: error frequency bounded away from zero; the ideal is approached only as delay grows (printed p.75). H > C: the equivocation floor H - C is inviolable by any encoding - 'Nature takes payment by requiring just that much uncertainty' (printed p.71). The existence proof is non-constructive: following it literally is generally impractical (printed p.74-75). Boundary H = C: points on the capacity line are in general not attainable (Fig. 9 discussion, printed p.71).

layer2.mapping: Install channel coach -> roster: C = reliable assignment-information bits per practice rep; the scheme is a source with entropy rate H (bits per snap of assignment detail). When H > C, blown-assignment equivocation >= H - C is guaranteed regardless of effort or talent - a capacity diagnosis, not a motivational one. Remedies are exactly the theorem's two levers: lower H (simplify the scheme, keep redundant structure) or raise C (more reps, clearer signals). Repetition across snaps is the block length that lets error frequency approach zero.
layer2.telemetry: Assignment-error counts per install volume (mental errors, missed checks, protection busts) charted against rep counts and scheme complexity; estimate the error floor vs install rate curve and compare to the H - C prediction. Internal practice/game charting only.

primitives.name: Theorem 17 - Shannon-Hartley capacity of a band-limited channel with white thermal noise under average power limitation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 17: The capacity of a channel of band W perturbed by white thermal noise of power N when the average transmitter power is limited to P is given by C WI P+N This means that by sufficiently involved encoding systems we can transmit binary digits at the rate W log2 P t N bits per second, with arbitrarily small frequency of errors. It is not possible to transmit at a higher rate by any encoding system without a definite positive frequency of errors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C = channel capacity, bits/s; W = bandwidth, Hz (cycles/s); P = average transmitter (signal) power, watts; N = average white thermal noise power, watts; P/N = signal-to-noise ratio, dimensionless; log_2 = binary logarithm. Dimensional check: W [1/s] times dimensionless log gives bits/s. The source writes the fraction (P+N)/N (OCR of the displayed fraction reads 'P t N'); entropy derivation H(y) = W log 2*pi*e*(P+N), H(n) = W log 2*pi*e*N (printed p.100) subtracts to the stated C.
primitives.assumptions: Signals and noise band-limited to W; noise is white thermal (Gaussian, flat spectrum) and additive, independent of the signal; average power constraint P on the transmitted ensemble; capacity-achieving input is a white-noise-like Gaussian ensemble of power P (printed p.100-101); arbitrarily small error frequency requires encoding delay T -> infinity (random noise-sample codebook, printed p.101).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Peak instantaneous power constraint instead of average: different bounds (Theorem 20, printed p.104-107, C > W log(2/(pi*e^3)) * S/N at peak S). Arbitrary non-Gaussian noise: only bounds W log((P+N_1)/N_1) <= C <= W log((P+N)/N_1) with N_1 the noise entropy power (Theorem 18, printed p.102). Low-SNR regime P/N -> 0: capacity approaches the linear wideband limit (P/N)*W/ln 2. Finite delay leaves a positive error frequency.

layer2.mapping: Game-day call-transmission channel: W = tempo bandwidth (plays/minute available for new information), P = signal power (clarity and reliability of the call/signal system), N = noise power (crowd noise, fatigue, substitution confusion). C = W log2(1 + P/N) bounds the rate of reliably executed novel calls. A no-huddle raises W but simultaneously raises N; net capacity can fall while symbol rate rises - the kernel is derived by instantiating the power-constrained channel on venue and tempo telemetry.
layer2.telemetry: Plays/minute, venue crowd-noise level (dB), delay-of-game / false-start / missed-check rates, substitution errors; fit effective N from error-rate vs noise curves and track C over game time. Internal telemetry only; no odds.

primitives.name: Theorem 13 - Sampling expansion for band-limited functions; 2TW degrees of freedom
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 13: Let f(t) contain no frequencies over W. Then ~ sin 7l'"(2Wt - n) j(t) = LJXn ( ) -00 7l'" 2Wt - n where In this expansion f (t) is represented as a sum of orthogonal functions. The coefficients X n of the various terms can be con- sidered as coordinates in an infinite dimensional "function space." In this space each function corresponds to precisely one point and each point to one function. A function can be considered to be substantially limited to a time T if all the ordinates X; outside this interval of time are zero. In this case all but 2TJV of the coordinates will be zero. Thus functions limited to a band Wand duration T correspond to points in a space of 2TlV dimensions.
primitives.latex: f(t) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} X_n\,\frac{\sin \pi(2Wt - n)}{\pi(2Wt - n)}, \qquad X_n = f\!\left(\frac{n}{2W}\right)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f(t) = signal amplitude at time t, arbitrary signal units u (e.g. volts or pascals); t = time, seconds; W = band limit, Hz (cycles/s); n = integer sample index, dimensionless; X_n = sample ordinate f(n/(2W)), units u; sample spacing 1/(2W), seconds; 2TW = number of degrees of freedom for duration T seconds and band W, dimensionless count. The sinc kernel sin(pi(2Wt-n))/(pi(2Wt-n)) is dimensionless; the series is an orthogonal expansion in function space (printed p.86).
primitives.assumptions: f(t) contains no frequencies above W (strict band limitation); exact reconstruction uses the infinite sample series; for duration T, all but 2TW coordinates are zero only when the function is 'substantially' time-limited (ordinates outside the interval zero, printed p.86). Energy-limited functions of band W and duration T lie in a 2TW-dimensional sphere of radius sqrt(2WE) (printed p.86).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Not band-limited: sampling aliases out-of-band energy into the reconstruction - structured error, not averaging noise. Strict time-limitation and strict band-limitation cannot both hold; the 2TW count is asymptotic ('substantially limited'). Sampling below rate 2W loses information irrecoverably. The source defers full rigor to the 1949 IRE paper 'Communication in the Presence of Noise' (footnote, printed p.86).

layer2.mapping: Player trajectories are continuous signals: a tracking system must sample above twice the motion bandwidth W or the reconstructed state aliases. A T-second play window carries 2TW degrees of freedom per player; 22 players plus ball set the dimension budget any Coach-Mind state encoder must respect. Claims of 'complete' field representation at sub-Nyquist rates are false by the theorem, not by opinion - the isomorphism is between band-limited function ensembles and band-limited motion ensembles.
layer2.telemetry: Optical/radio tracking (x, y, t) at known sample rate; estimate motion bandwidth from the trajectory spectrum; verify sample rate > 2W and quantify reconstruction error on held-out windows. Internal tracking data only.

primitives.name: Theorem 22 - Rate for a white noise source relative to an R.M.S. fidelity criterion (rate-distortion kernel)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 22: The rate for a white noise source of power Q and band W 1 relative to an R.M.S. measure of fidelity is Q R = WI log N where N is the allowed mean square error between original and recovered messages.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R = minimum rate of generating information at the given fidelity, bits/s; W_1 = message ensemble bandwidth, Hz; Q = average message power, u^2 (squared signal units); N = allowed mean square error between original and recovered messages, u^2; Q/N = dimensionless power-to-distortion ratio; log_2 binary logarithm. Dimensional check: Hz times dimensionless log = bits/s. General-source bounds (Theorem 23, printed p.115): W_1 log(Q_1/N) <= R <= W_1 log(Q/N) with Q_1 the entropy power of the source, u^2.
primitives.assumptions: Message ensemble is white (Gaussian) noise of power Q and band W_1; fidelity measured by mean square discrepancy; N < Q; the fidelity-evaluation representation v(P(x,y)) = integral P(x,y) rho(x,y) dx dy requires ergodicity and a 'reasonable' evaluation that converges on long samples (printed p.109-110). Rate defined as R_1 = min R subject to v = v_1 (Theorem 21, printed p.112).
primitives.breakdown_regime: N >= Q: rate collapses to zero (no transmission needed). Non-white or non-Gaussian sources: only the Theorem 23 bounds hold, not equality. Exact recovery of a continuous source requires infinite capacity (printed p.108), so any finite-rate representation is necessarily lossy. The variational solution P_y(x) = B(x) exp(-lambda rho(x,y)) is formal and 'difficult to evaluate in particular cases' (printed p.114).

layer2.mapping: A scouting report / tendency model / compressed game-state vector is a lossy code of the opponent-behavior ensemble: Q = variance of the behavior modeled, N = mean-square tolerance the staff accepts, R = minimum description rate. The kernel forbids a finite playbook that reproduces opponent behavior exactly and prices every compression choice: at fixed R, shrinking the representation forces N up as Q/N = 2^(R/W_1). Deception raises the effective N the defense must tolerate; the offense's own reports must buy N back with R.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction error of predicted routes/positions vs tracking truth (mean square, in m^2); report/model description length vs prediction-error curve to locate the achieved (R, N) point; compare against the W_1 log(Q/N) bound. Internal data only.

reasoning_traces.think:
Begin from the invariant, not the sport. Shannon's Theorem 2 (5ebcc3f3acfef4c9:p1, printed p.49-51) fixes entropy H = -sum p_i log p_i as the unique measure satisfying continuity, monotonicity under equiprobable refinement, and the grouping axiom. The source is explicit that this is a property of the ensemble, not of any single message: the system must be designed for every possible selection, since the actual selection is unknown at design time (printed p.31). Layer 1 therefore forbids any reading in which a single play 'contains' a fixed amount of information; information is a rate over a distribution of calls. Layer 2 binds this to the 22-player dynamical system by treating the offensive call sheet as a finite-state Markoff source (p1): states are down, distance, field zone, hash, personnel; the emitted symbol is the concept. The entropy rate H = sum P_i H_i (printed p.53) is then an auditable number in bits per call, estimated from internal charting, never from sportsbook prices.

The second invariant is the equivocation identity R = H(x) - H_y(x) (p2, printed p.67) with capacity C = max[H(x) - H_y(x)] (printed p.70). Shannon's coin-flip argument (printed p.67-68) is the veto against naive accounting: subtracting the raw error count (1000 - 10 = 990 bits/s) is wrong because it ignores where the errors are; when output is independent of input, half the symbols are 'correct' by chance and the true rate is zero. Transposed: a quarterback who checks to a hot route against a disguised shell may be 'right' half the time by luck; the correct metric is the conditional entropy of the true coverage given the pre-snap look, not the completion percentage on those plays. The confusion matrix of (pre-snap shell, post-snap revealed coverage) is the channel transition table p_i(j); its conditional entropy is the equivocation the defense has manufactured.

Theorem 11 (p3, printed p.71) then supplies the hard boundary. If the scheme's entropy rate H exceeds the install channel capacity C, no amount of coaching effort can drive the equivocation below H - C. This converts 'we keep blowing assignments' from a motivational diagnosis into a capacity diagnosis: either reduce H (simplify the scheme, exploit redundancy) or raise C (more reps, clearer signals). Theorem 17 (p4, printed p.100) adds the game-day constraint: C = W log2(1 + P/N). Crowd noise raises N; a no-huddle tempo raises W but also raises N through fatigue and substitution errors; the net capacity can fall even as the symbol rate rises. The high-EV deep shot that requires a complex protection call is therefore vetoed when measured C has collapsed, regardless of its nominal expected value, because the error floor H - C is information-theoretic, not effort-dependent.

Finally the delay clause matters: Shannon's existence proof averages over random codes and requires long blocks (printed p.71-75). In football terms, approaching capacity requires repetition across many snaps - the install is the block length. A scheme seen for the first time on a critical down is a length-one code: its error probability is bounded away from zero no matter how talented the roster. The sovereign reading is that play-calling is source coding under a noisy-channel constraint, and every aggressive call must be priced against the current equivocation floor, not against a highlight-reel payoff. The redundancy result (English roughly 50 percent redundant, printed p.56) closes the loop: keeping structured redundancy in the call language is not waste, it is the error-correcting margin that lets the roster decode under noise.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The hidden state in this book was created by a specific historical scar: the economics of telegraph and telephone bandwidth. Weaver's footnote (printed p.3, PDF p.10) traces the lineage Boltzmann 1894 entropy-as-missing-information, Szilard 1925, von Neumann 1932, then Nyquist 1924/1928 and Hartley 1928 at Bell Labs, into Shannon 1948, with Wiener's parallel statistical-filtering philosophy acknowledged on both sides. Hartley's logarithmic measure was chosen because engineering parameters - time, bandwidth, relay count - scale linearly with the logarithm of the number of possibilities (printed p.32). The unit 'bit' is Tukey's coinage (printed p.32). Nothing here originates in sport; the football binding is a declared Layer-2 isomorphism, not an origin story, and the genealogy matters because it explains why the theory measures freedom of choice rather than meaning.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Under pressure three belief models collide. The head coach's comfort call is a low-entropy symbol from his personal prior: high probability, low surprise, but also low information against a defense that has charted the same tendency. The defensive coordinator's trap is engineered equivocation: he shows a shell whose transition probabilities p_i(j) deliberately mislead, raising H_y(x) for the quarterback's read channel. The quarterback's internal clock is a finite-delay decoder: he must emit a throw before the block length - the protection - expires. Recursive modeling: the DC knows the coach knows the tendency; the QB must model the DC's model of his own read. The capacity theorem says this recursion cannot be resolved by cleverness alone when H exceeds C, only by changing the source statistics or the channel itself.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Physics vetoes psychology here in a precise sense. Suppose film study says a complex shot play has the highest expected payoff in the playbook. Theorem 11 still imposes equivocation at least H - C whenever the scheme entropy rate exceeds install capacity, and Theorem 17 says crowd noise and fatigue shrink C late in the game. The cross-layer adjudication: the psychological 'trust your gut' call is overruled by the information-theoretic error floor; the correct decision is to reduce H by calling from the low-entropy, high-redundancy subset until measured assignment-error rates fall. No motivational intervention can lower a floor that is a theorem about channels. The veto is quantitative: estimate C from reps and error telemetry before approving the high-EV call.

reasoning_traces.think:
The second cluster of invariants governs representation: how much of the continuous game can be captured, compressed, and reconstructed. Theorem 13 (5ebcc3f3acfef4c9:p5, printed p.86) states that a function band-limited to W is completely determined by samples spaced 1/(2W) apart, and that functions of band W and duration T correspond to points in a 2TW-dimensional space. Layer 1 is a statement about function spaces; Layer 2 binds it to player tracking: a trajectory is a continuous signal, and the tracking system's sample rate must exceed twice the motion bandwidth or the reconstructed state aliases. The dimension count 2TW is the budget any Coach-Mind state encoder must respect: ten seconds of a 5 Hz band-limited trajectory carries 100 degrees of freedom per player, and 22 players plus the ball multiply that budget. Claims of complete field representation at lower sample rates are false by the sampling theorem, not by opinion.

Theorem 22 (p6, printed p.115) is the rate-distortion kernel: for a white Gaussian message of power Q and band W_1, the minimum rate to reproduce it within mean-square error N is R = W_1 log2(Q/N). Theorem 23 extends this to bounds for arbitrary sources via entropy power. Transposed: a scouting report, a tendency model, or a compressed game-state vector is a lossy code of the opponent's behavior ensemble. Q is the variance of the behavior being modeled; N is the tolerance the coaching staff accepts; R is the minimum description length per second of game. The theorem forbids the fantasy of a finite playbook that reproduces opponent behavior exactly: exact recovery of a continuous source requires infinite capacity (printed p.108). Every game plan is therefore a rate-distortion point, and the honest audit question is which N was purchased at which R.

Weaver's Levels B and C (printed p.4-5, 26-27) supply the deception layer. He explicitly proposes semantic noise and a semantic receiver as additions to Shannon's diagram, and notes that overcrowding the audience's capacity produces general and inescapable error and confusion - the H > C regime transposed to meaning. A disguised coverage is semantic noise injected into the quarterback's decoder; a motion-heavy shift overload is an attempt to push the defense's semantic channel past capacity. The English-redundancy result (roughly 50 percent, printed p.56) explains why natural-language play calls survive crowd noise: residual redundancy is error-correcting structure, exactly Shannon's observation that unremoved redundancy helps combat noise (printed p.75).

For portfolio construction the same algebra applies without any odds input: a lineup slate is a code over the ensemble of game outcomes, and redundancy across lineups is the error-correcting structure that survives tail events. Theorem 15's entropy-power inequality (printed p.96) - the entropy power of a sum lies between the sum of entropy powers and the sum of actual powers - is the formal reason diversification cannot be scored by adding variances naively when components are dependent. The sovereign discipline is to measure Q, N, and R from internal telemetry - tracking reconstruction error, report length versus prediction error - and to refuse any claim of lossless compression of a continuous, adversarial source. The fidelity-evaluation machinery (printed p.109-110) adds the audit rule: any reasonable fidelity criterion must be expressible as an average distance over the joint source-output ensemble, so a staff's 'eye test' is legitimate only insofar as it converges on long samples to such an average.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The representation theorems descend from a different scar than the coding theorems: the problem of specifying continuous speech and television signals with finite hardware. Shannon cites his own 1949 paper 'Communication in the Presence of Noise' for the sampling expansion (printed p.86 footnote), and the fidelity-evaluation machinery (printed p.109-110) was built because exact transmission of a continuous source is impossible over any finite-capacity channel. The rate-distortion definition R_1 = min R subject to v = v_1 (Theorem 21, printed p.112) is the historical answer to the engineering budget question 'how much fidelity can we afford?', later transposed here to scouting and state-encoding budgets. No sport origin is claimed; the lineage runs through Nyquist's telegraph speed factors and the PCM/PPM bandwidth-for-SNR exchanges named in the introduction (printed p.31).
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The decoder's theory of mind is adversarial: the offensive coordinator models the defensive coordinator's model of his own tendencies, and chooses motions and formations to maximize the defense's equivocation per snap. The defense, symmetrically, allocates its finite semantic capacity - Weaver's audience-capacity analogy (printed p.27) - across the offense's message ensemble, knowing it cannot cover every possible call. Recursive belief clash: the QB knows the shell is a lie with some probability; the DC knows the QB knows; the play-caller exploits the DC's expectation of the exploit. The rate-distortion frame makes this tractable: each side is choosing a lossy code of the other's behavior, and the side with the better Q/N budget at fixed R wins the representation war.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The veto here is against over-compression. An analytics staff may propose a tiny state vector - three features per player - as sufficient for the Coach-Mind simulator. Theorem 13 vetoes this if the omitted motion bandwidth carries decision-relevant energy: aliasing is not noise that averages out, it is structured error. Theorem 22 prices the proposal: at fixed description rate R, shrinking the representation forces N upward as Q/N = 2^(R/W_1); the physiological layer adds that human working memory - the coaches' semantic channel - has its own capacity ceiling, so an over-dense report produces Weaver's inescapable confusion rather than marginal gains. The adjudication: reject the compressed state until tracking-reconstruction telemetry shows N within the staff's tolerance.

universal_lens: Audit lens: decompose every information claim into source entropy, channel equivocation, and capacity before accepting it. Distinguish absolute from coordinate-relative measures: continuous entropy shifts by the expected log-Jacobian under reparameterization (printed p.90-91), so only entropy differences - rates and capacities - are invariant. Any metric that changes when you rename coordinates is not a physical quantity; demand the invariant form.
gsi_mapping: GSI lens: neural spike trains and axonal signaling are band-limited ensembles in the sense of Theorem 13, so sampling and dimension budgets apply to electrophysiology telemetry; sensory decoding is an equivocation channel H_y(x) between stimulus and percept. The Shannon-Hartley power constraint maps onto metabolic signaling budgets (ATP turnover limits firing rate and bandwidth), and EEG band-power analysis is entropy-power accounting in the sense of Theorem 18. Fluid/axonal shear injury is channel damage: it raises N and lowers C, measurable as slowed or noisier conduction rather than vague fatigue.
gse_mapping: GSE lens: Coach-Mind sim consumes p1's call-source entropy, p2's coverage-read equivocation kernel, and p3's install-capacity constraint as hard gates on call approval; deception is modeled as injected equivocation (disguise) and semantic-noise overload (motion). DFS/portfolio tail risk is managed through redundancy and entropy-power diversification bounds, never through sportsbook odds. All artifacts remain internal; the engine queues decisions but never publishes, sends, or deploys them.
